subject: economics

concepts.title: Barter System and Double Coincidence of Wants
concepts.definition: An economic framework where goods are traded directly for other goods without a medium of exchange, requiring both parties to have exactly what the other desires.
concepts.key_idea: Direct exchange of commodities requires matching mutual needs.
question_patterns: What is a barter system?
Explain the concept of double coincidence of wants
Why is barter exchange difficult in large economies?
What are the drawbacks of a barter economy?

solution_steps.explain: Check if goods are being traded for goods or money.
Determine if both parties possess the specific good the other wants simultaneously.

concepts.title: Relative Price Calculation
concepts.definition: The value of one commodity expressed in terms of another, derived by comparing their monetary prices.
concepts.key_idea: Money acts as a unit of account to compare the worth of different goods.
question_patterns: Calculate the relative price of a pen worth {price_a} in terms of pencils worth {price_b}
How many units of good B is good A worth?
Find the exchange value of two goods given their prices

solution_steps.action: Divide price of first good by second
solution_steps.explain: The ratio of nominal prices gives the relative value.

concepts.title: Bank Net Worth
concepts.definition: The residual value of a financial institution calculated by subtracting its total liabilities from its total assets.
concepts.key_idea: Accounting identity where assets must balance with liabilities and equity.
question_patterns: Calculate the net worth of a bank with assets {assets} and liabilities {liabilities}
Find the equity of a firm given its balance sheet totals
What is the net worth if a bank has loans and reserves totaling {assets}?

solution_steps.explain: Net worth is the difference between what the bank owns and what it owes.

concepts.title: Money Multiplier
concepts.definition: The ratio that determines the maximum amount of broad money the banking system generates with each unit of reserves.
concepts.key_idea: The inverse of the reserve requirement dictates credit expansion capacity.
question_patterns: What is the money multiplier if the CRR is {reserve_ratio}?
Calculate the credit multiplier for a reserve ratio of {reserve_ratio}
How much can the money supply expand given a reserve requirement?

solution_steps.explain: The multiplier is the reciprocal of the cash reserve ratio.

concepts.title: Total Credit Creation
concepts.definition: The total volume of deposits created by the banking system starting from an initial primary deposit.
concepts.key_idea: Initial deposits lead to multiple rounds of lending limited by reserves.
question_patterns: Find the total deposits created from an initial deposit of {initial_deposit} with CRR {reserve_ratio}
Calculate the total money supply increase from a new deposit
How much total credit can a bank create with {initial_deposit} reserves?

solution_steps.action: Divide initial deposit by reserve ratio
solution_steps.explain: Total expansion is the initial injection times the multiplier.

concepts.title: Narrow Money (M1)
concepts.definition: The most liquid measure of money supply, including physical currency and demand deposits available for immediate transactions.
concepts.key_idea: Sum of cash with public and net demand deposits in banks.
question_patterns: Calculate M1 if currency is {currency} and demand deposits are {demand_deposits}
Find the narrow money supply
What is the value of M1 given the components?

solution_steps.explain: M1 consists of currency held by public and net demand deposits.

concepts.title: Broad Money (M3)
concepts.definition: A comprehensive measure of money supply that adds time deposits to the narrow money (M1) base.
concepts.key_idea: Includes both highly liquid and less liquid bank deposits.
question_patterns: Calculate M3 given M1 is {m1} and time deposits are {time_deposits}
Find the broad money supply in the economy
What is the total aggregate monetary resource?

solution_steps.action: Add M1 and net time deposits
solution_steps.explain: M3 is the sum of narrow money and commercial bank time deposits.

concepts.title: Average Transaction Demand for Money
concepts.definition: The mean amount of cash an individual holds over a period to facilitate regular spending, typically half of the periodic income.
concepts.key_idea: Cash balances fluctuate from full income to zero between pay periods.
question_patterns: If a person earns {income} monthly and spends it evenly, what is the average cash holding?
Calculate the transaction demand for an individual with monthly salary {income}
What is the mean money balance for a worker earning {income}?

solution_steps.explain: Average holding is the midpoint between initial receipt and final expenditure.

concepts.title: Velocity of Circulation
concepts.definition: The frequency with which a single unit of currency is exchanged for goods and services within a specific timeframe.
concepts.key_idea: The speed at which money moves through the economy.
question_patterns: Find the velocity of money if transactions are {transactions} and money stock is {money_demand}
Calculate how many times money changes hands
What is the velocity of circulation in this economy?

solution_steps.action: Divide total transactions by money demand
solution_steps.explain: Velocity is the ratio of total flow of transactions to the stock of money.

concepts.title: Present Value of a Two-Period Bond
concepts.definition: The current market price of a bond determined by discounting its future interest payments and principal repayment.
concepts.key_idea: Bond prices move inversely to market interest rates.
question_patterns: Calculate the PV of a bond with coupon {coupon}, principal {principal}, and rate {rate}
Find the market price of a 2-year bond
What is the present value of a bond given its returns and interest rate?

solution_steps.explain: Divide the first year return by (1 + r).

solution_steps.action: Discount the second year total return
solution_steps.explain: Divide the sum of coupon and principal by (1 + r) squared.
The total present value is the sum of all discounted future cash flows.

concepts.title: Speculative Demand for Money
concepts.definition: The desire to hold cash instead of interest-bearing assets based on expectations of future interest rate changes.
concepts.key_idea: Money demand increases as interest rates approach their expected lower bound.
question_patterns: Calculate speculative money demand given r={r}, r_max={r_max}, and r_min={r_min}
Find the demand for money for speculative purposes
What is the speculative demand at interest rate {r}?

solution_steps.explain: Subtract current rate from maximum expected rate.
Subtract minimum expected rate from current rate.
The ratio represents the speculative demand function.

concepts.title: Central Bank Policy Tools
concepts.definition: Instruments used by the Reserve Bank to regulate the volume of money and credit in the economy.
concepts.key_idea: Quantitative (CRR, Bank Rate) and Qualitative (Moral Suasion) tools control liquidity.
question_patterns: What are the instruments of monetary policy?
Explain Open Market Operations
How does the Bank Rate influence money supply?
Define Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the tool is quantitative (affects volume) or qualitative (affects direction).
Increasing rates or selling bonds typically reduces money supply.
